Sales & Account Health

Corporate Account Health Score — American Airlines

A 0–100 health score for managed corporate accounts, built to flag accounts drifting away before it's too late — giving sales managers a clear list of who to call first.

Why I built this

I've been an AAdvantage member for a while and American is genuinely my go-to airline. When I saw a Reporting Analyst role open there, it caught my attention immediately — building reports that help sales teams see which accounts are growing, which need attention, and where the opportunities are is exactly the kind of work I want to be doing.

The problem

American Airlines manages hundreds of corporate accounts through programs like AAdvantage Business. Accounts don't announce when they're about to leave — they quietly book less and shift spend to a competitor. By the time it's obvious in the data, the relationship is already at risk. Sales teams need an early warning system.

What I built

A Corporate Account Health Score in SQL Server and Power BI, scoring every account 0–100 based on year-over-year spend change, premium cabin booking frequency, recency of travel, and AAdvantage Business enrollment — turned into something a sales manager can act on Monday morning.

Note: built with synthetic data for portfolio purposes only — does not represent real American Airlines customers or data.

Healthcare Revenue Cycle

Claims Denial & Revenue Cycle Analysis

An RCM performance dashboard that moves billing teams from "handle each denial one by one" to a clear view of which payer, and which root cause, to fix first.

Why I built this

Healthcare organizations sit at the intersection of clinical excellence and financial complexity, where a single denied claim can quietly erode the revenue that funds patient care. I built this to demonstrate exactly the kind of work Clinical Shared Services teams need most: moving from raw billing data to clear, operational decisions, fast.

The problem

When claims get denied, practices don't get paid — and most billing teams lack a clear picture of which insurer denies the most, why, or how long money has sat uncollected. Denials get handled one at a time instead of fixing the root cause.

What I did

Analyzed denial patterns and root causes, tracked how long money sat uncollected, and built a dashboard so the client could open it and immediately see what's going wrong and where to focus — using SQL Server for the data and Power BI to visualize it.

Key insights
  • BlueCross BlueShield had the highest denial rate at 28%, putting $39,372 in revenue at risk.
  • Dr. Maria Lopez and Dr. Sarah Kim had the most denials among all providers, 17 each.
  • The most uncollected revenue past 90 days was tied to BlueCross claims — $5,391 from Dr. Priya Nair alone.

Note: built with synthetic data for portfolio purposes only — does not represent real patient, provider, or insurer data.

Capital Planning · Utilities

Capital Project Planning & Spend Tracker — MA Gas Business

A single source of truth for a 20-project capital portfolio, unifying financials from SAP-style data with field work status so leadership can see budget risk before it compounds.

Why I built this

When I came across a Capital Planning Analyst role, I wanted to understand the kind of data that team actually deals with — how do you track which of dozens of active projects is over budget, which have crews that haven't started, and which need a conversation with leadership? That question pulled me in enough to build the answer myself.

The problem

The Capital Planning team tracks dozens of active gas infrastructure projects at once, each with its own budget, crew, and timeline. Financial data lives in one system, work-order status in another — with no single place to see both together. Analysts spend hours every week manually reconciling data just to answer basic questions, and by the time the picture is assembled, it's already out of date.

What I built

A Capital Project Planning and Spend Tracker in SQL Server and Power BI simulating a 20-project portfolio across five work categories and five districts. Three SQL views handle project health, work-order execution, and portfolio totals, so business logic lives in the database. The dashboard has three pages: portfolio overview, a financial health tracker with conditional formatting that flags overruns instantly, and an operational performance page comparing planned vs. actual field hours.

Note: built with synthetic data for portfolio purposes only — does not represent any real National Grid project or business relationship.

eCommerce · Inventory & Demand

Amazon Demand & Inventory Tracker

A demand-forecast-inventory tracker for 20 products across five brands, built to catch stockouts and excess cash sitting on shelves before they cost real money.

SQL ServerPower BISQL Views
Why I built this

When I came across an eCommerce analyst role, I wanted to understand the kind of data that team works with day to day. Managing dozens of Amazon products at once is no small task — how do you know which are about to run out, which are overstocked, and which forecasts you can trust? I decided the best way to answer that was to build it myself.

The problem

Selling on Amazon is a constant balancing act: run out of a popular product and you lose the sale (and search ranking) for good; buy too much and cash sits stuck in inventory racking up storage fees. Sales, forecasts, and inventory usually live in separate places, so these problems get caught too late.

What I built

A demand and inventory tracker in SQL Server and Power BI, with a year of weekly sales, forecast, and inventory data for 20 products across five brands. Calculations like forecast accuracy, weeks of cover, lost revenue, and excess cash all live in SQL views. A three-page dashboard covers an executive overview, demand/forecast accuracy, and inventory risk, with slicers by brand and quarter.

Note: built with synthetic data for portfolio purposes only — does not represent any real Shurtape data or business relationship.
